cases.description: The record part of a reference is always singular, so a reference declared cardinality: many whose record does not exist is ref-dangling, while one into a record that exists and matches nothing is ok with no targets (§8.2, §8.5, decision I1.8).

A reference with a fragment into a record with a structural error cannot be resolved; it is not dangling but a ref-target-unreadable warning, at the $body that holds the link (§8.5, decisions I1.9 and J3).
An x-vmd-ref without targets allows any target: a record, a node, an asset and a directory (§9.3, decisions I1.11 and J6).
With targets, a reference outside them is ref-target-not-allowed, for contrast (§9.3).
In refs, a reference with a fragment into a record with a structural error has the status unreadable and no targets (§8.5, decision J3).
A reference with no fragment to a record with a structural error names the record, which exists, so it is ok with the record's root as its target (§8.5, decision J3).
The same reference raises no ref-target-unreadable warning in check, since its status is ok (§8.5, decision J3).
A reference with # alone also addresses the record's root (§7.1), so into a record with a structural error it is ok with the root as its target, like one with no fragment (§8.5, decision J3).

Resolving the root of a record with a structural error still fails, since a resolve returns the node's value, while refs gives a reference to that root the status ok (§8.5); the record's structural error is the issue, as for every operation that needs a value view.
